topic: Cash Flow Problems Don't Mean a Failing Business
objective: Reassure business owners that cash flow strain is common and manageable, not a sign of failure.

slides.headline: What does it mean?
slides.body: It's easy to read a cash-flow crunch as a sign something's wrong. In reality, many profitable, growing businesses hit cash-flow pressure simply because of timing — money going out faster than it comes in. Recognising this early makes it far easier to manage.

caption:
A cash-flow squeeze can feel alarming, but it's one of the most common challenges business owners face — and it doesn't necessarily reflect the underlying health of the business. Growth, seasonality and payment timing all create pressure that has nothing to do with profitability.

What matters is recognising the pattern early and having a plan, whether that's tightening collection terms or using short-term finance to bridge a gap.
